name: nav-rail
title: Nav rail
description: A slim vertical rail of icon destinations with tooltips, badges, a top slot and a pinned bottom group, for apps with many areas.
docs: items is the list of areas: { id, label, icon, href, badge, badgeLabel, group }. icon is an element (<IconHome />), label is the tooltip, the label under the icon and the accessible name, and an area with an href is a link while one without is a button. current is the id of the area you are in: it is filled and marked aria-current='page'. onSelect(id) is called when one is chosen; on an area with an href a plain click goes to it and a modified click opens the address. badge is a number (the NotificationBadge count: hidden at 0, '99+' above 99) or true for a dot, and badgeLabel (default 'updates') says what it stands for, so a screen reader hears 'Messages 3 unread messages' for a count and 'Reports New report' for a dot: the label comes first in the markup and is drawn after the icon. Entries that follow each other with the same group sit together, and a thin rule is drawn where the group changes. top holds the brand mark; bottom is pinned under the list, for settings and the account, and NavRailItem (label, icon, href, current, onSelect) makes entries there that match the rest. The list is a plain ul inside a nav landmark (label, 'Main' by default), so Tab walks it. On a short screen the list scrolls on its own and top and bottom stay in place, with room inside the scroller for the focus ring. showLabels widens the rail and puts each name under its icon, so the tooltips are not needed. expandOnHover keeps the rail's width and slides a labelled panel over the content when the pointer is over it or focus is inside it, so nothing shifts; expanded holds that panel open. Reduced motion shows it without the slide.
